sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 34.8% a year from $404.5 million in FY2016 to $5.93 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].

The path was a step change, not a smooth compound: growth of 64.2% in FY2021 [D218] collapsed to 11.8% in FY2022 [D263] and 0.1% in FY2023 [D311], then recovered to 16.4% in FY2024 [D358] and 10.6% in FY2025 [D406].
The FY2017 loss of $3.45 billion [F32] was driven by a $2.6 billion increase in stock-based compensation, primarily the CEO award and RSUs tied to the IPO [P74].
Operating margin has improved every year since FY2017's -422.5% [F22], reaching -9.0% in FY2025 [F30], a 5.7pp gain on FY2024 [D419][F29].
FY2025 revenue rose $570.0 million, with advertising up $282.4 million on roughly 17% more impressions and other revenue up $287.6 million on subscriber growth [P24].
Other revenue contributed 5.4pp of FY2025 growth and reached 12.6% of revenue, up from 4.3% in FY2023 [D545][D543][D539].
North America remains the largest geography at 58.6% of revenue but contributed only 4.4pp of FY2025 growth, against 3.7pp from Rest of world [D456][D458][D499].
Operating costs grew 5.5pp slower than revenue in FY2025 [D430], at 5.1% [D423], and the incremental operating margin was 44.8% [D429].
Diluted shares rose 2.1% in FY2025 [D425], so the 35.7% smaller EPS loss [D410] outpaced the 34.0% smaller net loss [D408].
FY2025 operating margin of -9.0% [F30] sits above the -32.4% window median [D555] and is the window high [D554].
The 5.7pp FY2025 improvement [D419] came from cost of revenue (+1.1pp) [D431], R&D (+1.3pp) [D432] and other lines (+3.3pp) [D433].

Sales and marketing fell $42.4 million on the timing of marketing events and lower advertising, partly offset by higher headcount [P22], while R&D rose $101.9 million on product development headcount [P23].
In FY2025 net margin of -7.8% [F50] sat 1.2pp above the -9.0% operating margin [F30], helped by $68.9 million of other income [X130] that included $96.7 million of debt-extinguishment gains [P18].
FY2025 operating cash flow of $656.2 million [F80] exceeded the $460.5 million net loss [F40], and free cash flow was $437.2 million, a 7.4% margin [F100][D393].
Operating cash flow was driven by the net loss adjusted for $1.0 billion of stock-based compensation and $163.6 million of D&A, plus working-capital timing [P13].
Capex of $219.0 million [F90] was 3.7% of revenue [D392] and 1.34x D&A [D395].
Stock-based compensation of $1,016.8 million [X90] was 155.0% of operating cash flow [D396], so cash generation still depends on a non-cash add-back.
Cash and investments of $2.94 billion [D397] against total debt of $3.54 billion [D398] leave net debt of $596.3 million, net cash of -10.1% of revenue [D399][D400].
That is the 0th percentile against an internet peer median of 45.0% net cash of revenue (n=5) [D578][D579], and the current ratio of 3.56x is the window low [F180][D565].
The FY2025 debt moves were a $1.4 billion repurchase of 2026-2028 notes funded by $1.50 billion of new 2033 Notes [P1][P2].
Buybacks of $750.9 million [X156] were 171.7% of free cash flow [D402], and the diluted share count still rose 2.1% [D425].
Net losses have persisted for all 10 years, from $514.6 million in FY2016 to $460.5 million in FY2025 [R1][F31][F40].
The loss is narrowing but ten straight years of red ink means profitability still rests on non-GAAP adjustments rather than the income statement [R1].
Stock-based compensation was 17.1% of revenue in FY2025 and at least 10% in each of the last nine years [R2][D390].
At $1,016.8 million [X90] it exceeds the operating loss, so reported margins understate the real cost of compensation [R2].
Net cash fell for four straight years into net debt of $596.3 million in FY2025 [R3][D399].
Buybacks of $750.9 million [X156] at 171.7% of free cash flow [D402] while the balance sheet is in net debt is the capital-allocation risk to watch [R4].
Whether operating margin in the FY2026 10-K holds above the -9.0% FY2025 level [F30] would confirm the cost discipline described in FY2025 [P15].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue in the FY2026 10-K moves back above the -10.1% FY2025 level [D400] would reverse the four-year slide into net debt [R3].
Whether stock-based compensation falls below the 17.1% of revenue recorded in FY2025 [D390] would show the dilution pressure easing.
